summary: The main article describes an asymmetric 1,4-functionalization of 1,3-enynes using dual photoredox and chromium catalysis. It includes 1 table for reaction optimization, 5 figures detailing substrate scope and mechanistic studies, and references to product characterization in the Supplementary Information.

items.heading: Fig. 1
items.caption: Catalytic asymmetric 1,4-functionalization of 1,3-enynes. a Transitionmetal catalyzed asymmetric 1,4-functionalization of 1,3-enynes. b This work: radical 1,4-functionalization of 1,3-enynes by dual photoredox and chromium catalysis. Rad alkyl radical precursors.
items.description: Comparison between traditional transition-metal catalyzed ionic pathways and the newly developed radical-involved dual catalytic pathway for 1,3-enyne functionalization.

items.heading: Fig. 2
items.caption: The importance of chiral allenols. Bn benzyl, TBS tert -butyldimethylsilyl, Me methyl, TIPS triisopropylsilyl, Et ethyl, Tol p -methylphenyl, t -Bu tert -butyl, Boc tert -butoxylcarbonyl.
items.description: Illustrates the structural significance and utility of chiral allenols in the synthesis of complex molecules and natural products.

items.heading: Table 1
items.caption: Reaction optimization
items.description: Optimization table showing the effects of different catalysts, ligands, solvents, and conditions on the yield and stereoselectivity of the 1,4-functionalization.

items.heading: Fig. 3
items.caption: The scope of aldehydes in the 1,4-functionalization of 1,3-enynes. a 2.0 equiv of DHP ester and 2.0 equiv of 1,3-enyne were used. iPr isopropyl, Bpin boronic acid pinacol ester, Ac acetyl.
items.description: Displays the variety of aromatic, heteroaromatic, and aliphatic aldehydes compatible with the reaction conditions.

items.heading: Fig. 4
items.caption: The scope of DHP esters and 1,3-enynes in the 1,4-functionalization of 1,3-enynes. a 4-( tert -butyl)-2,6-dimethyl-1,4-dihydropyridine-3,5-dicarbonitrile was used as radical precursor. b 3.0 equiv of corresponding 1,3-enyne were used. c The yield is for allenol product, and the minor regioisomer refers to the propargylation product from the 1,2-functionalization. TMS trimethylsilyl, TES triethylsilyl.
items.description: Explores the compatibility of different radical precursors (DHP esters) and 1,3-enyne derivatives in the three-component coupling.

items.heading: Fig. 5
items.caption: Exploration of other radical precursors and representative synthetic applications. a RBF3K as the radical precursor. b Redox-active ester as the radical precusor. c Desilylation and cyclization. NBS N -bromosuccinimide.
items.description: Demonstrates the use of organotrifluoroborates and NHPI esters as radical sources, along with downstream synthetic transformations of the products.

items.heading: Fig. 6
items.caption: Mechanistic investigations. a Radical trapping experiment. b Light on/off and quantum yield mearsurement. c TheStern -Volmer plot. d Proposedmechanismfor the 1,4-functionalizaton of 1,3-enynes.
items.description: Provides experimental evidence for the radical pathway, including trapping experiments, light-dark cycles, and a proposed catalytic cycle.
